instruction: Turn off Chrome's Safe Browsing feature entirely. I want to disable all website safety warnings.

parameters.command: echo {CLIENT_PASSWORD} | sudo -S apt update -y && echo {CLIENT_PASSWORD} | sudo -S apt install jq -y

mkdir -p /home/user/.config/google-chrome/Default && if [ ! -f /home/user/.config/google-chrome/Default/Preferences ]; then echo '{}' > /home/user/.config/google-chrome/Default/Preferences; fi && cd /home/user/.config/google-chrome/Default && jq '. + {"safebrowsing":{"enabled":false,"enhanced":false}}' Preferences > temp && mv temp Preferences

metadata.explanation: Task requires disabling Safe Browsing (opposite of original). Reuses existing get_enable_safe_browsing getter with expected value 'false'.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter logic is correct: get_enable_safe_browsing checks BOTH safebrowsing.enabled and safebrowsing.enhanced flags, returning 'false' only when both are disabled
Instruction coverage is complete: The instruction requires turning off Safe Browsing 'entirely', and the getter correctly verifies that both enabled and enhanced protections are disabled
Expected value is semantically correct: Expected 'false' (string) matches the requirement that Safe Browsing should be completely off
Metric is appropriate: exact_match correctly compares boolean string values ('true' vs 'false')
Postconfig is necessary and correct: Chrome restart ensures Preferences file is written and settings take effect before verification
No state timing issues: Getter reads from Preferences file on disk which is persisted after Chrome restart
